hints.title: Cubic Substring Check Obstacle
hints.text: Testing every possible substring for duplicate characters takes cubic time. How can you extend a contiguous valid segment to the right and only contract the left boundary when a duplicate appears?

hints.title: Dynamic Window Boundary Jump
hints.text: Maintain an expandable contiguous range [left, right]. When character s[right] was already seen at index j >= left, jumping left directly to j + 1 restores uniqueness in constant time.

hints.title: Sliding Window with Last-Seen Map
hints.text: Iterate through s with index right, recording the most recent index of each character. If the current character was previously seen at or after left, advance left to that character's last seen index + 1. Update the maximum length with right - left + 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (0 <= N <= 5 * 10^4)
M: size of character set (M <= 128 for ASCII or 256 for extended)
complexity.notes: Each character is processed once. Auxiliary hash map size is bounded by the alphabet size M.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all O(N^2) substrings with an O(N) duplicate check takes O(N^3) time. For N = 5 * 10^4, this takes over 10^13 operations, timing out immediately.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing the last seen position of each character in an O(M) table allows jumping the left boundary forward in O(1) time instead of shrinking character by character.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling boundary jump condition (last_seen[ch] >= left), edge cases like empty string, all identical characters, and all distinct characters, achieving O(N) time.

solutions.approach: Sliding Window with Last-Seen Index Map
